### ADR-1: Target platform: web / PWA only (no store app)

- Context: The React app replaces the OutSystems mobile app (Cordova, 21 native plugins in the survey: FCM push, Crashlytics, TouchId, Barcode, Location, SocialSharing, File/FileTransfer/FileViewer, InAppBrowser, PrivacyScreen, ScreenOrientation, Keyboard, LocalNotification, AppLauncher, EventfulDeeplinks, AndroidAppLinks). Options were web first + Capacitor later, Capacitor from the foundation, or web/PWA only.
- Decision: Web / PWA only (user, 2026-10-14). UI stays HTML/CSS 1:1. Native features go behind adapters in src/lib/device with web equivalents decided per feature in the behaviour inventory (extras group C).
- Consequences: No app-store build. Per-feature web equivalents to decide: push (Web Push; iOS only for installed PWAs, 16.4+), biometric unlock (WebAuthn), barcode (camera + JS library), share (Web Share API), files (download/open), in-app browser (new tab), deep links (URLs + manifest), crash reporting (web monitoring). PrivacyScreen, orientation lock and keyboard control have no full web equivalent. Service worker (Workbox) comes with production integration, not in the mock phase.

### ADR-2: Baseline: current stable dependency versions before scaffolding

- Context: Scaffold pins 2024 versions (React 18.3, Vite 5.4, React Router 6.26, TS 5.6, MSW 2.4, Node 20 which is end of life since 2026-04-30). The app replaces production; nothing is built yet.
- Decision: Upgrade the baseline before scaffolding (user, 2026-10-14: React 19, Node 24 LTS, current stable Vite, React Router, TypeScript, MSW, test and lint tools). Exact versions are chosen from the npm registry, checked together in a scratch install (typecheck, build, tests), listed for the user, then pinned with dep add.
- Consequences: The foundation owner adapts scaffold_react_app.py output to the new majors once (router, MSW, test setup). Version list needs the user's acceptance before dep add.

### ADR-3: Third-party libraries for OutSystems modules and OSUI providers

- Context: Build screens use Leaflet (BrowseDirectory, CountryDetails), SortableJS (Services), ReactiveHtmlSanitizer (MessageDetail, Notifications, Photobook) and OSUI patterns with provider libraries: Carousel (Splide), DropdownSearch (Virtual Select), RangeSlider (noUiSlider + wNumb). Versions read from TST file headers 2026-10-14.

### ADR-4: Tooling for the API contract (group A) and the component catalog (group D)

- Context: User chose extras A (OpenAPI contract with OutSystems action names, MSW validates against it) and D (Storybook catalog, CI, docs) on 2026-10-14.
- Decision: Proposed: openapi-typescript (types from the contract) + openapi-fetch (typed client); Storybook for the shared blocks; CI as a platform-neutral npm run ci script (no platform chosen, git init only when the user asks).

### ADR-8: Bookmark sync replaces the local bookmarks in one IndexedDB transaction

- Context: SynchBookmarks / SynchBookmarksC2 (app start, via Sync_Info_GetMain) run DeleteAll then CreateOrUpdate as two IndexedDB transactions in the original (OutSystems.js deleteAll -> executeTransaction). A screen that reads LocalBookmark between the two steps sees no bookmark (menu shows Bookmark instead of Unmark). On TST the first screen reads before the sync starts; in the clone the first screen loads right after the GetUserInformation step, so its read lands inside the sync (HouseholdDetails default parity, F4a 2026-10-15). Known original race: known-original-bugs.md B5.
- Decision: Keep the clone's entityService.replaceAll: delete and re-create the bookmark rows in one transaction (app/src/shell/localEntities/entities.ts:230, localBookmarks.ts:200-225). Recommended by the orchestrator; auto-accepted under the user's auto mode (2026-10-15 16:59) and listed for the user's review.
- Consequences: Deviation from the 1:1 rule (bugs included): a read during the sync now sees either the old or the new rows, never none. No visible change on TST timing. Revert = two transactions again plus a timing exemption on HouseholdDetails default.

### ADR-9: PWA: installable online-first app with a Workbox service worker (vite-plugin-pwa injectManifest)

- Context: ADR-1 fixes web/PWA only; stack pwa said no service worker in the mock phase. The user decided the PWA plan on 2026-10-16 (migration/pwa/pwa-discussion-plan.md section 7: P1 online-first, P2 injectManifest, P3 caching table 3a, P4 TST manifest values + browser default install prompt, P11 silent update, P13 iOS 16+ degrade, P16 app SW only in non-mock builds). TST manifest fetched (migration/runtime-sources/UBTConnect.pwa-manifest.json). Versions by the stable rule (major line >= 9 months, version >= 60 days, checked 2026-10-16): vite-plugin-pwa 1.3.0 (1.x since 2025-03-29; 2.0.0 is from 2026-10-03, too young; peer vite ^7), workbox-* 7.4.1 (7.x since 2023-05-31; 7.4.1 from 2026-05-04).
- Decision: Add vite-plugin-pwa 1.3.0 (dev) and workbox-build 7.4.1 (dev); workbox-window, workbox-core, workbox-precaching, workbox-routing, workbox-strategies, workbox-expiration 7.4.1. Own SW file (injectManifest) built and registered only when VITE_USE_MOCKS=false; mock/demo builds keep MSW and unregister a stale app SW. Manifest = TST values (name/short_name Connect 2.0, standalone, theme #1992ab, background #ffffff, TST icons 48-512, start_url and scope /UBTConnect/, portrait), browser default install prompt only. Caching per table 3a: precache hashed bundles + original per-screen CSS + fonts; navigations network-first with the precached index.html fallback; original images cache-first 30 days; never API, signed photos, /bff/*, auth callback, network-ping. Silent update: the new SW waits for the next cold start (no skipWaiting); forced reload only when the API contract version changes (hook ready, wired with the BFF). Offline keeps the original toasts (no offline screen).
- Consequences: Parity and captures keep blocking service workers; PWA behaviour gets its own Playwright e2e (P14, phase 5). Two build modes to document (mock with MSW, production with the app SW). iOS: no install prompt, separate storage, features degrade without errors. Push, WebAuthn, BFF auth and the barcode scanner come in later phases with their own ADRs.

### ADR-10: Personal data in IndexedDB: documented exception to stack tokens

- Context: Stack tokens: never in browser storage. The original (TST) keeps notes, bookmarks, search history, recent searches and Orbit local entities in IndexedDB; the clone does the same (app/src/shell/localEntities, ADR-8). The user decided P10 on 2026-10-16: keep it as the original.
- Decision: Client entities stay in IndexedDB as in the original. Tokens, PIN and identity secrets are never stored in browser storage (unchanged). When installed, call navigator.storage.persist(); after an eviction, re-sync from the server; clear all local entities on logout. Only the shell stores touch browser storage (rule NO-BROWSER-STORAGE unchanged for routes).
- Consequences: Personal data at rest on the device, as today in TST; the privacy notice must mention it. Safari may evict data of non-installed sites; every screen must work after an eviction.

### ADR-11: Vendor the TST BarcodePlugin web scanner (OSBarcodePlugin.js) for PWA scanning

- Context: PWA decision P7 (user, 2026-10-16): vendor the TST scanner. The original BarcodePlugin, without Cordova and with navigator.mediaDevices, loads OSBarcodePlugin.js (html5-qrcode + ZXing web scanner, BarcodeDetector when supported, rear camera) (migration/runtime-sources/BarcodePlugin.controller.js:21-94, 201-203). The clone answers CheckBarcodePlugin 'not available' (OS-PLUG-BARC-0011) and registers a fictional scanner in the mock phase (OrbitAdminEventDetail Q1 = A). Rule: libraries the original ships keep the TST version.
- Decision: Vendor migration/runtime-sources/BarcodePlugin.OSBarcodePlugin.js unchanged (as ADR-5/7), with its CSS as AddCSSJS injects it, behind a device adapter (src/lib/device, named by ADR-1). Port CheckBarcodePlugin / ScanBarcode web branches 1:1. Production uses the web scanner; dev and demo keep the fictional scanner by default (Q1 = A) and use the web scanner with ?scanner=web.
- Consequences: Needs HTTPS (or localhost) and camera permission; iOS has no BarcodeDetector, so ZXing decodes. The vendored file is third-party code (html5-qrcode and ZXing, Apache-2.0 per its headers, to verify) with no npm updates; upgrades follow TST.

- Context: PWA decision P14 (user, 2026-10-16): Playwright PWA e2e + manual device matrix + Lighthouse CI; parity keeps blocking service workers. ### ADR-13: Lighthouse runs through the lighthouse package 13.4.1 instead of @lhci/cli

- Context: ADR-12 chose @lhci/cli 0.15.1 for Lighthouse CI. Its scratch install fails npm audit with 11 high advisories from its own tree (tmp, extract-zip, basic-ftp/proxy-agent, puppeteer-core, inquirer, bundled lighthouse 12.6.1); 0.15.1 is the newest release (PWA-5T report 2026-10-16). lighthouse 13.4.1 (13.x since 2025-10-10, 13.4.1 from 2026-07-20) passes the stable rule and a scratch audit shows 0 vulnerabilities.
- Decision: Replace @lhci/cli by lighthouse 13.4.1 (dev), driven by a small Node script (npm run lighthouse) with the ADR-12 scope: demo build served statically, HomeFeed / Search / OrbitLanding at mobile emulation, performance, accessibility, best practices, warning budgets, local filesystem output only (never uploaded).
- Consequences: No LHCI server or assertion DSL; the script implements the budgets. Same Chrome requirement as the e2e suite.

### ADR-14: Production service worker served at TST's worker URL /UBTConnect/pwaServiceWorker.js (cutover handover)

- Context: PWA fact F2 (user, 2026-10-17): TST registers /UBTConnect/pwaServiceWorker.js on scope /UBTConnect/. It is cache-first for every screen path from its precache, and old caches are deleted only by a newer worker (migration/knowledge/pwa-tst-service-worker.md). Browsers re-check the registered script URL; if it answers 404 after cutover, devices keep the cached OutSystems app. P15 decided a same-origin cutover with a service-worker handover. Options: (A) serve our own worker at that URL; (B) a kill switch at that URL, then the new index.html registers /sw.js.
- Decision: Option A (user, 2026-10-17): production builds serve the app service worker at /UBTConnect/pwaServiceWorker.js with scope /UBTConnect/, instead of /sw.js. Browsers update the existing registration in place on their next update check. On activate, the worker deletes the OutSystems caches (names starting with UBTConnect-).
- Consequences: Production SW URL and output path change (src/pwa/swRoutes.ts SW_URL, build/pwa.ts, src/sw/sw.ts activate cleanup, tests, docs/guides/pwa.md). The URL must keep answering from cutover on (never 404). The worker file stays under /UBTConnect/, not at the root of the origin shared with ConnectMobile. The demo build is not covered by this ADR (own host). Implementation is phase 5 work.

### ADR-15: Target front-end architecture (refactor-plan-v2)

- Context: The React app passes parity with OutSystems on all 64 routes, but its folders follow the OutSystems structure (`screens/`, `shared/`, `shell/`). Plan v2 §7 counts 71 files that call `callAction` outside `api/`, 50 users of `getClientVar` and a 1,077-line component file. The goal is code that a team can keep in production, with the same UI and calls as the original. The user approved `app/docs/architecture/refactor-plan-v2.md` on 2026-10-22, with R1 to R8 as recommended and D1 to D4 of the draft (§9). Auto decisions Q1 to Q4 of the same day, accepted under the user's delegation, changed the tools (`migration/refactor/auto-decisions-2026-10-22.md`).
- Decision: Adopt the target architecture of `app/docs/architecture/refactor-plan-v2.md` §2 and §3 for `app/src/`. Plan v2 holds the full text; this ADR lists the decisions and points to the sections.
  - Terms (§2.1): a page renders one route, in `pages/<Route>/<Route>Page.tsx`, and does not import another page. A hook (`use*`) holds data, state or a flow and returns no markup. A container calls hooks and renders one component tree. A component renders UI from props, keeps only local UI state and does not call `api/`, `platform/`, flags or navigation. A layout in `components/layout/` places the header, content and bottom areas and does not fetch data.
  - Folders (§2.2): the router, the route table with meta and the providers go to `app/`. Each route has `pages/<Route>/` with its page and the `hooks/`, `components/` and `containers/` that only this page uses. Code that 2 or more pages use goes to `containers/`, `components/ui/`, `components/layout/` or `components/<domain>/`. Server calls go to `api/client/` and `api/<domain>/`, and app services go to `platform/<area>/` (auth, session, settings, flags, navigation, device, storage, bootstrap, feedback). Pure functions go to `lib/`, and the OutSystems compatibility code goes to `legacy/os/`, which gets smaller in each phase. `mocks/` stays unchanged, and `styles/` holds the tokens and the CSS layers.
  - Container criterion (§2.3, R2 b): hooks by default. Make a container only in two cases. First, one component tree renders data from two different sources. Second, the tree needs 2 or more data hooks and 3 or more event handlers, in a file of more than 200 lines. The column `shape` of `app/docs/refactor/move-map.csv` records the choice for each block.
  - Rules 1 and 2 (§2.4): new code starts in `pages/<Route>/`. When a second page needs the code, the code moves to `components/`, `containers/` or `api/`.
  - Rules 3 to 9 (§2.4, import direction): a page does not import another page, and only `pages/<Route>/` imports `pages/<Route>/` (P3-1, dependency-cruiser rule `pages-imported-by-own-route-only`). `components/**` does not import `api/`, `platform/`, `containers/`, `pages/` or `app/`, and `components/ui/` imports only `components/ui/`, `lib/` and `styles/`. `lib/` imports only `lib/`, and `api/<domain>/` imports only `api/client/`, `lib/` and `legacy/os/`. `platform/**` does not import `pages/`, `components/`, `containers/` or `app/`. Only `platform/`, `api/` and `app/` import `legacy/os/`.
  - P3-2 (decision Q11, auto-accepted under the user's delegation, 2026-10-22): story files (`*.stories.tsx`) and test files (`*.test.ts`, `*.test.tsx`) are outside the cycle rule and every folder rule in `app/.dependency-cruiser.cjs` (constant `STORY_OR_TEST`). Reason: the cycle came only from 8 UBTConnectLibrary stories. They render the real blocks of the captured screen (for example BottomBarMenu), and Storybook is a review tool that must show them. Production code keeps every rule.
  - P3-3: the only module cycle in `src/` (`platform/session/cachedUserInfo.ts` and `mockUser.ts`) is gone: the record type is in `platform/session/types.ts`.
  - P7-6 (decision W32, 2026-10-24): `src/shared/` is deleted, with its alias and the six dependency-cruiser rules that named it. Its files went by data owner. Block components went to `components/<domain>/`, `containers/DetailLayout`, `platform/session/UserInfoCache` and `legacy/os/cache/`. Pure helpers, structures and static entities went to `lib/<module>/`. MSW files went to `mocks/modules/`, and test helpers went to `src/test/`. The module client actions in `lib/<module>/actions.ts` still import `api/`, `platform/` and `legacy/os/`. Rule 6 has 55 warnings for them (follow-up F35). Since P9-1 a baseline freezes these rows.
  - F43 (decisions W38 and W39, 2026-10-24): `os-wire.ts`, `os-assets.ts` and `os-assets.manifest.json` are in `lib/`, as plan §2.2 says, not in `legacy/os/`. A codemod moved them; only import paths changed.
  - P9-1 (decisions W38, W39 and W41, 2026-10-24): every folder rule of §2.4 and `no-circular` is an error in `app/.dependency-cruiser.cjs`. Three baselines freeze the old violations and only shrink: `app/.dependency-cruiser-known-violations.json`, `app/docs/refactor/arch-baseline.csv` and `app/.knip-known-unused.json`. A new violation or a stale row fails `npm run ci`. `jscpd` has a threshold of 0.57 percent, and knip runs in `ci`. Rule 9 does not check mock handlers and test helpers. Follow-ups F35 to F37 and F46 to F50 own the rows.
  - P9-2 (decisions W42 and W43): `npm run flags` runs `app/build/check-flags.mjs` in `ci`. It fails on a registry key with no reader, an unknown key and a past `removeBy`. It also fails on a stale list entry and on a new flag reader outside pages, hooks and containers. Four readers are outside today: 1 by design and 3 owned (F35, F51, F52).
  - Restored views (F22 to F26, F39, F40): a flow hook of `useFlowState` runs OnInitialize on the saved state of a back navigation. `onParametersChanged` runs only when the parameters change. When the user left before the answer came, the port calls again. OutSystems keeps the skeleton (F40, an intended difference). F39 waits for the user. The recipe is `app/docs/guides/page-template.md`.
  - P4-1: `platform/settings` is the typed store of the server settings that `synchAppContext` writes. It has 11 settings, one more than plan §3.2 (`pin.inactivity.navigate`). The OutSystems names stay in the adapter `legacy/os/clientVarNames.ts`, which `getClientVar` and `setClientVar` use until the readers move with their pages.
  - P4-2: `platform/session/machine.ts` holds the session status and the events of §3.2. It has the pure `transition` and one unit test per row. The statuses are `starting`, `signedOut`, `signingIn`, `needPinRegister`, `locked`, `policiesPending` and `unlocked`.
  - P4-2 senders: `session.ts markAppReady`, `auth.ts` and `pin.ts` send the events. LockHost sends through `pin.ts lock()`.
  - P4-2 differences from §3.2: `isLocked()` and `hasUnlocked()` keep reading the stored `PIN_IsLocked` and `PIN_HasUnlocked`. The event `userChanged` is only for the mock identity provider. `signOut` also applies from `signingIn`. No event leads to `policiesPending` yet.
  - P4-3: `platform/auth` has the `AuthProvider` interface, `mockAuth` (imported behind `MOCKS_BUILT` only) and `authProvider()`. `platform/bootstrap/appStartSteps.ts` runs the app start as named steps (7 in P4-3, 8 since P4-5), and `postLogin.ts` holds the post-login calls. `build/mockFree.ts` has a production-only plugin, so `KNOWN_MOCK_LEFTOVERS` is empty.
  - P4-3 differences from §3.2: the file is `appStartSteps.ts`, not `appStart.ts` (case clash with `AppStart.tsx`). `fetchFlags` became a step in P4-5. `mockUser.ts` stays in `platform/session` until a later move step. A production build has no identity provider. Its sign-in shows "Sign-in is not available: no identity provider is configured." Dev, mock and demo builds sign in as before.
  - P4-5: `platform/flags` has the typed registry of 21 flags in `registry.ts`. These are the 20 flags of `flags.generated.json` and `mobileDirectoryLocalityContacts` (default off). The folder also has `resolve.ts`, `store.ts`, `overrides.ts`, `server.ts` and `useFlag`; the OutSystems names are in `legacy/os/flagNames.ts`. `FLAG_OVERRIDES_BUILT` (`platform/config`: dev, or a mock build) keeps `?ff=` and the panel out of a production build. The step `fetchFlags` comes after `synchAppContext` and makes no call in the mock phase: the values are the defaults.
  - P4-5 readers: `platform/flags/flags.ts` is an adapter (`useFlagOn`, `isOn`, `setFlag`, typed with `FlagKey`) for the 30 old readers, and the helpers in `UBTConnect_Utils/lib/actions.ts` call `flagValue`. The call sites keep their flag checks until Phase 6. The fields `kind`, `owner` and `removeBy` are `null`, and the check of P9-2 needs `removeBy`.
  - P4-5 differences from §3.1: `meta.flagRedirect` is on 6 routes (Notifications, Bookmarks, MyBookmarks, LDM_MyEvents_V2, HouseholdCarousel, SupperMeeting_Carousel), and `useOsNavigate` applies it. A URL that is opened directly is not redirected, the same as before. `capture-plan.json` has no flag variants, so parity covers the defaults and unit tests cover the on and off paths.
  - P5-1: `api/client/apiError.ts` has `ApiError` (`kind`: timeout, network, server, security, viewChanged; `cause`: the OutSystems exception), and `legacy/os/os-exceptions.ts` maps both ways. `callAction` is unchanged. `signedOutRemotely()` in `platform/session/auth.ts` is the single entry point for "the server ended the session" (machine event `signedOutRemotely`, same end state as `signOut()`). Today only the forced-logout branch of `platform/feedback/exceptionMessages.ts` calls it. The 401 and SecurityException triggers wait for the BFF (decision Q12, option C). The App_Common SecurityException branch is the known gap G1 in `migration/refactor/followups.md`.
  - Rules 10 and 11 (§2.4): no import cycle anywhere. Imports use the alias `@/`, not `../../..`. Since P1-4, ESLint reports a relative parent import as an error (`app/eslint.config.js`). `src/sw` is exempt. In `components/**` the pattern stays a warning, because rule 4 shares it.
  - Rule 12 (§2.4, R8 b): a barrel `index.ts` exists only at `components/ui`, `components/<domain>`, `containers`, `api/<domain>` and `platform/<area>`. Other code imports these folders through the barrel only.
  - Rule 13 (§2.4, R4 b): each file that ports an OutSystems screen or block has one `@origin` tag. Inline references to compiled line numbers (`mvc.js:640-1150`) go away when the file is rewritten, not before.
  - Naming and OutSystems blocks (§2.5, §2.6): business names in PascalCase without a module prefix, and hooks named `use<Thing>`. Each `api/<domain>/` has `repository.ts`, `mapper.ts`, `keys.ts`, `hooks.ts` and `types.ts`; wire types stay in `src/api/schema.d.ts`. A UI-only block becomes a component, and a block with data or side effects becomes a hook and a component. A screen becomes `pages/<S>/<S>Page.tsx`, a layout block goes to `components/layout/` and an OutSystems UI pattern goes to `components/ui/`.
  - State (§2.7): TanStack Query is the only server-state store, and every call goes through `api/<domain>/`. Query options in `api/<domain>/keys.ts` replace `memoryCache`, after an exemption list (§5.4). View state moves to `platform/navigation/viewState.ts`; pages and hooks use it, and components do not. Client variables split into `platform/settings`, `platform/session` and `platform/navigation`.
  - Styles (§2.8, R3 b): Phase 8 adds `styles/tokens.css` and puts the original CSS in `@layer legacy`. `styles/layers.css` sets the order `legacy, app` once. `StylesheetHost` loads each original file through a `<link>` to a `data:` stylesheet that only does `@import url(<file>) layer(legacy)`; the files stay unchanged. New CSS goes in `@layer app`. A future Content-Security-Policy must allow `style-src data:` (follow-up F44). Existing components keep the legacy class names and CSS, and new components use CSS Modules with the tokens. Unused CSS goes away one stylesheet at a time, with coverage data from the parity captures, at the `visual` level.
  - Feature flags (§3.1, R5 a): the `platform/flags` area has a typed registry, `resolveFlags` (precedence default < server < override) and `useFlag`. Only pages, hooks and containers read flags. The route table (`meta.flagRedirect`) handles the four flags that choose a screen. The app start waits for `fetchFlags()`. In production the flags come from one batch call through the BFF, with a parity exemption for the flag calls.
  - Session and PIN (§3.2, R6 a): a state machine in `platform/session/machine.ts` holds the session status, and the selectors keep their names. The `AuthProvider` interface in `platform/auth/` has the `mockAuth` implementation behind `MOCKS_BUILT`, and this refactor does not build `bffAuth`. The app start steps keep their calls, order and conditions, and `fetchFlags` is the only new step. PIN verification stays local, as in the original, and the security owner reviews it before the BFF phase.
    - Route guard: the route meta (`app/routes.ts`: `access`, `lock`, `flagRedirect`) and the one `RouteGuard` (`app/RouteGuard.tsx`, reads the session status) keep the redirect table of the old `startup.ts` unchanged. `platform/` does not import `app/`, so `LockHost` gets `ignoresLockScreen` as a prop.
  - Parity and API (§4.1, D1, D2): two parity levels, `strict` (all checks) and `visual` (no DOM checks), plus a self-parity reference. The API contract stays unchanged behind `api/<domain>/`.
  - Scope and sequence (R1 b, R7 b): phases 0 to 7 in about 50 days, and phases 8 and 9 as a stretch goal. Phase 2 builds a walking skeleton on HouseholdDetails before the mass work.
  - Tools (§4.4, D3 as changed by Q2 and Q4): dependency-cruiser checks rules 3 to 10 and exports the import graph. ESLint core `no-restricted-imports` checks rule 11. jscpd reports duplicate code, and knip reports unused files and exports. ts-morph runs the codemod `migration/tools/refactor/move.ts`.
  - Q5 (auto-accepted under the user's delegation, 2026-10-22): the 4 `DEPRECATED_*` OutSystems UI patterns stay as legacy UI components with business names in `components/ui/legacy/` (phase P7, shape `ui`). They are not deleted, because the DOM must stay the same (R3).
  - Q6 (auto-accepted under the user's delegation, 2026-10-22): the 5 `ContactByEmail*` pages share a `ContactEmailForm` and two card components. Each page has a config object and one submit hook, and there is no container. `EmailContact`, `EmailTarget` and `LDM_Email_V2` stay separate.
- Consequences: After the user accepts this ADR at the P0-5 gate, `stack.py dep add --dev --adr ADR-15` allows the packages below.
  - Dev dependencies to allow (stable rule, ADR-2; release dates in `app/docs/refactor/baseline.md`): `@vitest/coverage-v8` 4.1.12, `dependency-cruiser` 17.4.3, `jscpd` 4.3.0, `knip` 5.88.1 and `ts-morph` 27.0.2.
  - Security patches to allow under the ADR-2 security exception (decision Q3): `vite` 7.3.7, `vitest` 4.1.12, `storybook` 10.6.3 and `@storybook/react-vite` 10.6.3. They replace `vite` 7.3.6, `vitest` 4.1.11 and the two `storybook` packages 10.5.8 in the allow-list.
  - D3 changes by auto decision Q4: the refactor drops `eslint-plugin-boundaries`, and dependency-cruiser checks rules 3 to 9 because it resolves the `@/` alias. Decision Q2 adds no `eslint-plugin-import-x` and no `tsx`. ESLint core `no-restricted-imports` checks rule 11, and the codemod runs on plain Node 24. Plan v2 still names the dropped packages in §4.3 to §4.5, step P1-1 and the D3 row of §9. These places need a text update.
  - Accepted advisory: `braces` GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm (high, stack exhaustion on deeply nested patterns) has no patched version. It comes only through the dev-only CLIs `knip` and `jscpd` (through `fast-glob` and `micromatch`) and does not reach the app bundle. The only fix path, `knip` 6.42.1, fails the stable rule, and `jscpd` 4.3.0 keeps the path. Check the advisory again at Phase 9.
  - The refactor does not use `route.py` (D4). `migration/tools/refactor_parity.py` runs the parity at the level of each step, against the OutSystems captures and the self-parity reference. Self-parity exemptions go to `migration/refactor-exemptions.json` with the step id, the reason and the user's confirm.
  - Open point: the consistency rules of `stack.json` (`requiredFiles`, `requiredIfCalls`, `allowedImportRoots`, NO-ROUTE-CSS) describe the folders of the migration. They need a change before the code moves to the new folders.
  - Plan v2 §2.2 example "containers/ (ShareSheet, FilterSheet, BottomBar)" needs a text update: FilterSheet and BottomBar are not containers (no data action; `component` and `hook+component`).
  - The memoryCache readers (`CacheControl`, `CacheControl_*`, `CacheControl_UserInfo_Wrapper`) are rewritten in P5-4, where they are; P6 only moves the files.
  - OSBlock placement (decision Q7, auto-accepted): OSBlock and the other presentational OS* widgets go to `components/ui/os/`, not `legacy/os/widgets/`. They render the DOM that R3 keeps forever, so they are permanent UI primitives that rule 5 allows. A widget that imports from `legacy/os` (check OSPopup and OSValidation) stays in `legacy/os/` behind a platform adapter. Plan v2 P1-3 needs a text change (components/OS* → components/ui/os/). The move map has no `src/components/OS*` rows, so none was added.

### ADR-16: Remove noUiSlider and wNumb

- Context: Step F29 (commit 9b88da40) deleted the unused RangeSlider pattern and uninstalled the packages nouislider and wnumb. ADR-3 had allowed both for the RangeSlider pattern.
- Decision: Remove nouislider and wnumb from the allowed dependencies and remove the osui:RangeSlider item. ADR-3 stays as the record of the earlier decision (user, 2026-10-24).
- Consequences: ContactUsDetails does not use a range slider library. A new use of a range slider needs a new ADR and a version check.

### ADR-17: Vendor the TST Orbit Passport loader (OrbitPassportScanC2.PassportScan.js) for PassportScan

- Context: PassportScan Q1 (a) (user, 2026-10-29): vendor the TST loader. The original block `OrbitPassportScanC2.PassportScan.ScreenBlock_PassportScan` loads `OrbitPassportScanC2.PassportScan.js` as its JS dependency and calls `window.OrbitPassport.embed` from its JS nodes. The loader puts the portal page in an iframe and talks to it with `postMessage`. Rule: libraries the original ships keep the TST version.
- Decision: Vendor the TST file unchanged in `src/vendor/orbitpassport/` (byte-identical copy, version 1.0.0, as ADR-5, ADR-7 and ADR-11), behind a typed adapter (`src/vendor/orbitpassport/index.ts`). `SOURCE.md` of that folder records the URL, size and sha256. Upgrades follow TST.
- Consequences: The vendored file is third-party code with no npm updates. The file states no license: confirm it with the Orbit Passport portal owner before production. The portal origin must allow the iframe of the app host.
